bug_claim: The withdrawAll function passes [0, 0] as minimum withdrawal amounts to curvePool.remove_liquidity, meaning zero slippage protection. A sandwich attacker can manipulate pool reserves before the withdrawal to drain value from the position.
minimal_setup: Define pool constants: initial WETH reserve, initial OETH reserve, LP token supply
Define victim LP token balance representing the strategy's position
Compute expected fair withdrawal amounts at pre-attack spot price
Simulate attacker front-run: large WETH->OETH swap that tilts pool
Compute actual withdrawal amounts at post-manipulation spot price with zero minimum enforcement
Compute attacker back-run profit from restoring pool balance
No contract deployment needed - pure math simulation
constants: STRATEGY_LP = 200u128 (10% of pool, in WAD units)
ATTACKER_WETH = 500u128 (attack swap size, in WAD units)
test_steps: Step 1: Define constant pool state (balanced 1:1 Curve pool) with WETH=1000, OETH=1000, total_LP=2000
Step 2: Strategy holds 200 LP tokens (10% of pool)
Step 3: Compute fair_weth_out = (strategy_lp / total_lp) * pool_weth = 100 WETH expected
Step 4: Simulate attacker front-run: swap 500 WETH in for OETH. After swap: pool_weth = 1500, pool_oeth = 666 (using x*y=k invariant approximation)
Step 5: Recompute withdrawal at manipulated pool: actual_weth_out = (strategy_lp / total_lp) * manipulated_weth = 150 WETH, actual_oeth_out = (strategy_lp / total_lp) * manipulated_oeth = 66 OETH
Step 6: Compute WETH value of OETH shortfall: oeth_shortfall = fair_oeth_out - actual_oeth_out = 100 - 66 = 34 OETH lost
Step 7: Simulate attacker back-run: sells 150 WETH profit OETH back, restoring pool. Net attacker profit from manipulation = value extracted from strategy position
Step 8: Assert that with zero slippage (minAmounts=[0,0]), the actual OETH received (66) is far below the fair value (100), demonstrating the vulnerability
Step 9: Assert that if minAmounts were set to 99% of fair value (99 WETH, 99 OETH), the withdrawal would revert because actual_oeth=66 < 99, proving zero-slippage is the root cause

assertions.actual_buggy_value: 66 OETH (66 * WAD) received due to pool manipulation
assertions.explanation: With zero minimum amounts enforced, the withdrawal accepts 34% less OETH than fair value after attacker tilts pool
zero minAmounts means no lower bound check; any manipulated pool ratio is accepted

assertions.actual_buggy_value: false (transaction succeeds with current [0,0] minAmounts, value is extracted)
assertions.explanation: If minAmounts=[99*WAD, 99*WAD] (1% slippage), actual_oeth=66 < 99 would cause revert; current code passes [0,0] so no protection
